'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Pazigyi massacre]]
***At least 100 people are killed in an airstrike by the [[State Administration Council|military junta]] in the village of Pazigyi, [[Kanbalu Township]], [[Sagaing Region|Sagaing]], in the third major attack against [[civilian]]s since the junta's [[offensive (military)|offensive]] in Sagaing began in February. It is the junta's deadliest attack since seizing power in [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|2021]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/11/world/asia/myanmar-airstrike.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis (2021–present)|Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis]]
**Fighting occurs near the [[Armenia]]n village of [[Tegh]], resulting in the deaths of four Armenian and three [[Azerbaijan]]i soldiers. [https://apnews.com/article/nagorno-karabakh-armenia-azerbaijan-soldiers-af13054c5bbbe0c54437adc97b537de0 (Associated Press)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**Four [[Balochistan Police|police personnel]] and a [[terrorism in Pakistan|terrorist]] are killed in an [[shootout|exchange of fire]] during a [[Balochistan Police|police]] operation in [[Kuchlak]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://gnnhd.tv/news/20066/four-cops-martyred-during-kuchlak-operation (GNN)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**A [[Palestinian National Security Forces]] member and another [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] man are killed by [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] in [[Elon Moreh]], [[West Bank]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/11/israeli-soldiers-kill-two-palestinians-near-nablus (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Republican insurgency in Afghanistan]]
**The [[Taliban]] say that the [[313 Central Corps]] carried out an operation in [[Parwan Province]], killing eight rebels, including a commander, of the [[National Resistance Front of Afghanistan|National Resistance Front]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2285086/world (Arab News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] announces that Jews will be prohibited from visiting the [[Temple Mount]] for the remainder of [[Ramadan]], following [[2023 Al-Aqsa clashes|raids by Israeli forces]] on the [[al-Aqsa Mosque]] last week. [[Ministry of National Security (Israel)|National security minister]] [[Itamar Ben-Gvir]] condemns the decision. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2023/04/israel-bans-visits-jews-temple-mount-last-10-days-ramadan (Al-Monitor)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Richmond, Indiana facility fire]]
**A massive fire at a recycling plant in [[Richmond, Indiana]], sends plumes of toxic smoke into the air and forces the evacuation of about 2,000 people in a half-mile radius of the fire. [https://www.wpsdlocal6.com/news/indiana-recycling-plant-fire-forces-evacuation-orders-for-thousands-as-it-emits-toxic-smoke-officials/article_b1c6d2de-d926-11ed-bcb1-63813549eeee.html (CNN)]
*The [[Shiveluch volcano]] in the [[Russian Far East]] erupts, sending ash up to {{convert|20|km|miles}} into the air. [https://www.dw.com/en/volcanic-eruption-in-russias-kamchatka-threatens-aviation/a-65275061 (DW)]
*Hundreds of residents of [[Gangneung]], [[South Korea]], are forced to [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] and a person is killed as more than 2,300 [[Fire services in South Korea|firefighter]]s combat a spreading [[wildfire]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-korea-wildfire-gangneung-d8445ba0c79ef7fa295e9f878ccd198f (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*The [[World Health Organization]] reports the first death from [[H3N8]] in a 56-year-old woman in [[Guangdong Province]], [[China]], who died March 16. The virus has been circulating since 2002, when it first appeared in North American waterfowl. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/apr/12/china-records-first-h3n8-bird-flu-death-who-says (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Germany]] expels the [[ambassador]] of [[Chad]], [[Mariam Ali Moussa]], in a [[tit-for-tat]] decision following the expulsion of the German ambassador from Chad last week. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/germany-expels-chads-ambassador-tit-for-tat-move-2023-04-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sweden]] announces the indefinite closure of its embassy in [[Pakistan]]. [https://thepakistandaily.com/sweden-shuts-its-embassy-in-pakistan-for-indefinite-period/ (''The Pakistan Daily'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[President of Malawi|President]] of [[Malawi]] [[Lazarus Chakwera]] [[pardon]]s 200 prisoners, including a former minister [[criminal conviction|convicted]] of [[corruption]]. [https://www.nyasatimes.com/chakwera-pardons-uladi-mussa-199-other-prisoners/ (NyasaTimes)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Indonesian general election]], ''[[PRIMA v. KPU]]''
**The [[Jakarta]] High Court overturns a lower court's order to delay [[Indonesia]]'s national elections for two years. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-court-rule-appeal-against-order-delay-elections-2023-04-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022–23 NHL season]]
**In [[ice hockey]], the [[2022–23 Boston Bruins season|Boston Bruins]] break the NHL record for the most points scored in a single season with 133, surpassing the [[1976–77 Montreal Canadiens season|1976–77 Montreal Canadiens]]. This comes two days after winning their 63rd game, surpassing the [[2018–19 Tampa Bay Lightning season|2018–19 Tampa Bay Lightning]] and [[1995–96 Detroit Red Wings season|1995–96 Detroit Red Wings]] for the most wins in a regular season. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/boston/news/boston-bruins-set-new-nhl-points-record-133-points-regular-season/ (CBS Sports)] [https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/36164424/bruins-defeat-capitals-set-another-nhl-record-133-points?platform=amp (ESPN)]
